title: Creamy Fonio Cereal with Blueberries, Pomegranate and Brown Butter
author: Pierre Thiam
desc: Fonio simmered five minutes in salted water, stirred with warm milk, topped with blueberries, pomegranate and a spoonful of foaming brown butter.
longDesc: A breakfast porridge from ‘The Fonio Cookbook’. A cup of fonio, 2 cups of water and a teaspoon of salt boil on high, then simmer gently, covered, for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the water has been absorbed. The heat goes off and 2 cups of warmed milk (or full-fat coconut milk) are stirred in with a minute’s standing, then the optional brown sugar and cinnamon. Each bowl is topped with blueberries and pomegranate seeds, and the butter is cooked in a small pan until slightly brown and foamy and drizzled over.
ingredients: 2 cups milk or full-fat coconut milk, warmed
steps: Combine the fonio, water and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat, cover and simmer gently 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the water has been absorbed. Turn off the heat.
Stir in the warmed milk and let stand 1 minute. Stir in the brown sugar and cinnamon if using.
Divide among four bowls and top each with blueberries and pomegranate seeds.
In a small pan cook the butter until slightly brown and foamy. Drizzle over the fonio and serve.
chefTips: ‘Until the water has been absorbed’ is the porridge cue.
‘Slightly brown and foamy’ is the butter cue — a minute too long and it burns.
Vegan version: coconut milk and no brown butter, per the blogger.
Warm the milk first so the fonio doesn’t cool and seize.
commonMistakes: Adding cold milk to hot fonio.
healthBenefits: Fonio is gluten-free and easy to digest.
culturalNote: The blogger’s framing, drawn from the book: fonio is ‘an ancient grain that’s cultivated by small farms in West Africa’, with a delicate, nutty taste, low on the glycemic scale. It is not a Senegalese traditional breakfast as printed; the recipe is a modern one from the cookbook.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Creamy Fonio Cereal with Blueberries, Pomegranate, and Brown Butter’. PAGE BYLINE: ‘By Dara O’Brien, Creative Director, Lake Isle Press’. Credit line: ‘Recipe reprinted From ‘The Fonio Cookbook,’ by Pierre Thiam, Lake Isle Press, 2019.’ lakeislepress.com, no date printed. Yield: ‘Serves 4’. TWO-PASS on every quantity.
Cues, short fragments: ‘until the water has been absorbed’; butter ‘slightly brown and foamy’. No oven temperatures, no heat printed for the later steps.
Remarks from the blogger, not Thiam: fonio is sold at select grocers including Whole Foods; a vegan version works with coconut milk and omitting the brown butter.
